claims.explanation: Parachlorophenol is a phenolic antimicrobial that likely acts as a mitochondrial uncoupler/oxidative phosphorylation inhibitor and generates reactive oxygen species, so selectivity is driven by dependence on oxidative phosphorylation and by antioxidant capacity rather than by a single annotated target. Lines with KEAP1/NFE2L2 pathway mutations and high NRF2 antioxidant programs, or with low mitochondrial/ROS-buffering capacity, are expected to be most sensitive, while lines with intact antioxidant defenses and glycolytic metabolism are protected.

features.basis: KEAP1 loss impairs NRF2 degradation and alters redox balance, increasing vulnerability to phenolic ROS/electrophile stress; KEAP1-mutant lines (NCIH1623, HEC265) appear among extremes
Constitutive NRF2 activation raises antioxidant capacity and would blunt parachlorophenol-induced oxidative damage; NFE2L2-mutant lines (SNUC5, TE6, KYSE520, HEC265) are enriched among least affected
Loss of p53-mediated stress/apoptosis checkpoints can increase sensitivity to cytotoxic phenolic stress; TP53 mutation is common in the most-killed lines
STK11/LKB1 loss impairs AMPK-linked metabolic stress responses and mitochondrial homeostasis, favoring sensitivity to metabolic/oxidative poisons; seen in NCIH1623, TE4, KALS1
SMARCA4 loss creates chromatin/transcriptional stress vulnerability; SMARCA4-mutant lines (SKNSH, OV7, KYSE270) are among the most killed
FBXW7 loss stabilizes oncoproteins and impairs stress-induced degradation, potentially increasing sensitivity to cytotoxic stress; enriched in killed lines (CL11, SNUC5, NCIH1648, MKN1)
ALK-altered neuroblastoma/lung lines (NCIH2452, KELLY, SKNSH) are among the most killed, suggesting ALK-driven lineages have metabolic dependencies sensitive to the drug
EGFR-mutant lung lines (HCC4006, KYSE270) appear among the most killed, possibly reflecting oncogene-driven metabolic/redox dependencies
BRAF-mutant melanoma and colorectal lines (K029AX, SH4, IGR37, WM793, LS1034) are enriched among least affected, suggesting MAPK-driven glycolytic/antioxidant programs protect against the drug
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling and is enriched in least-affected lines (BT549, HEC265, WM793, HS766T), consistent with protection from cytotoxic stress
ARID1A-mutant lines (MDAMB175VII, HEC265, MHHNB11, T47D, HS766T) are enriched among least affected, suggesting SWI/SNF-altered chromatin states can buffer the drug response
KMT2D loss is enriched in several most-killed lines (BICR6, SNUC5, KYSE270), possibly reflecting epigenetic stress vulnerability
